The paper investigates the application of ROM to solidification problems.
The authors use a 1D heat equation test case to demonstrate the effectiveness of ROM.
The 1D heat equation test case uses a rectangular function as the initial condition.
The singular values of the 1D heat equation test case decay exponentially fast.
The advection reference case uses a step function as the initial condition.
The singular values of the advection reference case decay slowly.
A steep slope in the advected quantity leads to a slow decay of singular values.
The presence of a mushy zone in alloy solidification improves the quality of ROMs.
The pressure component decays faster than the velocity component in metal solidification problems.
A pressure ROM can be used to speed up numerical fractional step algorithms.
The paper uses a 2D solidification test case to demonstrate the effectiveness of ROM.
The 2D solidification test case uses a unit square domain.
The Boussinesq approximation is used to solve the 2D solidification test case.
The implicit pressure correction scheme is used to solve the 2D solidification test case.
The authors use a radial basis function (RBF) interpolation to infer the right singular values.
The paper uses a deep neural network to map the right singular values.
The authors use a Smolyak sparse grid to avoid an extensive amount of snapshots.
The paper uses a Taylor-Hood (continuous P2-P1) element to solve the 2D solidification test case.
The authors use an Adams-Bashforth projected convecting velocity and Crank-Nicolson for the convected velocity.
The paper uses a temperature-dependent mix of solid and liquid to model the mushy zone.
The authors use a 5000 snapshot matrix to collect the solution snapshots.
The paper uses a 171 snapshot matrix to capture 99.99% of the energy in the case with a mushy zone.
The authors use a 1527 snapshot matrix to capture 99.99% of the energy in the case without a mushy zone.
